examples.label: positive
negative

value.reason: In routes/resetPassword.ts, line 42 loads the full User record with UserModel.findByPk(data.UserId) and no attributes filter. Line 46 then sends the updated model back with res.json({ user: updatedUser }). Sequelize turns the whole instance into JSON, so the response includes every column defined in models/user.ts: the password column (stored as the output of security.hash, a weak hash per the weakPasswordChallenge marker), role, lastLoginIp, profileImage and the other redacted fields, which in this model are likely the deluxeToken and totpSecret columns. The exposure is marked Public, and password reset is normally reached without being logged in. That means an unauthenticated caller can get back the password hash and other sensitive account fields that a reset confirmation doesn't need. This matches the positive example (findByPk followed by res.json of the whole model) and not the negative one (an attributes allow-list or derived values only). It is a case of Broken Object Property Level Authorization and a lack of reasonable safeguards for personal data.
